seoTitle: How to Send Automatic Emails in Jira
metaDescription: Set up Jira notification schemes and automation rules to send automatic emails for issue creation, status changes, and assignments.
intro: Manually notifying teammates about every issue update wastes time and gets missed. This guide walks through configuring Jira's notification schemes and automation rules so automatic emails go out for events like issue creation, status changes, or assignments.

steps.heading: Open your notification scheme
steps.body: Go to your Jira project settings and locate the notification scheme controlling which events trigger emails.

steps.heading: Set up automation rules for emails
steps.body: Create an automation rule that triggers on a specific event, such as issue creation or a status change, and add a send-email action.

steps.heading: Configure recipients and content
steps.body: Choose who should receive the automated email and customize the message so it includes relevant issue details.

steps.heading: Test the automatic emails
steps.body: Trigger the event manually to confirm the email sends correctly and reaches the intended recipients.

steps.heading: Avoid email overload
steps.body: Limit automated emails to meaningful events so your team doesn't get overwhelmed by notifications.

faq.question: Do I need admin permissions to set this up?
faq.answer: Yes, configuring notification schemes and automation rules typically requires project or Jira administrator access.

faq.question: Can I customize the email template?
faq.answer: Yes, Jira lets you customize the content and formatting of automated emails within the automation rule or notification settings.

faq.question: Will automatic emails work for all issue types?
faq.answer: Yes, you can scope automation rules to specific issue types or apply them across all issues in a project.

faq.question: How do I stop unwanted automatic emails?
faq.answer: You can disable or edit the specific automation rule or notification scheme entry that's triggering the unwanted emails.
